response.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT P.ID, P.SEX, AVG(L.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(L.IGA - L.IGM) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory L JOIN Patient P ON L.ID = P.ID GROUP BY P.ID, P.SEX), o AS (SELECT AVG(avg_diff) AS m FROM p) SELECT p.SEX, AVG(p.avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(p.avg_diff) AS avg_iga_igm_diff, AVG(p.avg_diff / o.m) AS avg_ratio FROM p CROSS JOIN o GROUP BY p.SEX

assumptions.assumption: The 'mean across all patients' is the mean of the per-patient IGA−IGM averages, so each patient counts once. Patients with no non-null IGA−IGM value are excluded from it.
The IGA−IGM difference is computed per record, so a record with a missing IGA or IGM has no difference and is ignored. The sex-level figures are unweighted averages of the per-patient values.

alternatives.interpretation: The overall mean is taken over all matched lab records (record-weighted), not over the per-patient averages.
